chunks: God’s Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever is pleased with his good deeds and feels bad about his bad deeds is a believer.

key_terms.سَاءَتْهُ: It displeases him / He feels bad about it
key_terms.سَرَتْهُ: He is pleased with it / It pleases him

ai.seo_question: What is the defining characteristic of a true believer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a definitive internal criterion for faith, linking the believer's spiritual state to their self-awareness and moral sensitivity. This emotional responsiveness—joy in virtue and sorrow in vice—serves as a practical indicator of sincerity (ikhlas) and is often interpreted by Shia scholars as a manifestation of the 'light of faith' illuminating the heart. It underscores that true belief is not merely declarative but is validated by the heart's natural reaction to one's own conduct.
